architecture_decision.reason: The live RAID1 root is a single ext4 filesystem with no dm-crypt layer or spare partition. Preallocated LUKS2 files provide strong block encryption for selected domains without repartitioning or reformatting the live root and allow staged, reversible migration.

vault_layout.contents: all authoritative user, project, course, media, studio, portal, release, recording, ingress and security asset directories
Redis persistent state plus retained sanitized application and Docker logs
local backup_data artifacts and retained restore evidence
Docker image layers, writable layers and json-file logs after authoritative named volumes move to explicit encrypted domain mounts
operator/application secrets, retained system journals and classified release/audit state; unlock keys remain external

not_selected.option: retrofit full-root LUKS or repartition md0
not_selected.reason: requires destructive live-root migration or reinstallation and violates the no-live-disk-reformat constraint

not_selected.option: one monolithic vault for every data class
not_selected.reason: couples unrelated service lifecycles and creates an unnecessarily large availability and rollback blast radius
requires live filesystem feature and per-directory policy changes while leaving swap, Docker layers and logs as separate exposures
does not transparently cover PostgreSQL WAL, Redis, logs, swap and container writable-layer spill

not_selected.option: persistent unlock key on the same unencrypted root
not_selected.reason: would defeat the offline disk and provider-snapshot threat model

must_protect_against: offline theft or loss of either RAID member
offline provider or hypervisor snapshot of the root filesystem
accidental copying of local application data without the external unlock material
offline inspection of closed vault files
does_not_claim_protection_against: a live root compromise while vaults are unlocked
application authorization defects after data is legitimately decrypted
malware executing as a service identity with access to its mounted vault
plaintext deliberately exported by an authorized user or operator
full-disk encryption of the operating system or boot partition

key_management.recovery_key_location: operator-owned encrypted storage outside the production host
key_management.header_backup_location: off-host and separate from the vault file
rotation_order: create a new off-host recovery key
back up the current LUKS2 header
add the new key to an unused slot
prove open and read integrity using the new key
remove the superseded key only after independent recovery verification
key_management.lost_last_required_key_result: unrecoverable-data incident; never auto-delete the last verified keyslot

boot_and_service_contract.current_mode: manual operator unlock after boot using external material
boot_and_service_contract.systemd_gating: dedicated aionex-encrypted-storage target plus RequiresMountsFor/After dependencies
boot_and_service_contract.missing_key_behavior: affected services remain stopped and systemd records a critical local failure; no plaintext fallback directory
boot_and_service_contract.unexpected_reboot_behavior: system boots, encrypted-data services remain unavailable until an operator unlocks and verifies vaults
boot_rehearsal_before_live_migration: open each candidate vault from external recovery material
verify ownership, checksums and expected empty-underlay guard
close and reopen in a maintenance rehearsal without rebooting the live host
boot_and_service_contract.owner_alert_pre_cutover_requirement: prove an owner-visible out-of-band alert path that does not depend on the locked vault

FR-06C: redis_data or a proved ephemeral reconstruction contract
journald/system logs that may contain application metadata
rebuildable_exclusions: security_tool_cache_data after inspection for user excerpts

per_vault_sequence: record exact source volume identity, size, file count and checksum manifest
take a fresh encrypted R2 recovery point and validate it
preallocate and format a new LUKS2 vault using external keys
copy while source services remain running only for a nonauthoritative pre-seed
stop only services that write the selected domain
perform final delta copy and integrity comparison
mount the encrypted target and bind it through explicit Compose configuration
start only scoped services and run health plus functional verification
retain the original source read-only for the rollback window
wipe the original plaintext only after owner-visible acceptance and a second recovery proof
rollback: verify database/assets and record the failed encrypted candidate without deleting evidence

performance_acceptance.production_gate: each later vault requires a workload-specific immediate baseline and encrypted candidate comparison with no integrity error and no more than 15 percent p95 regression

scope_boundary.next_action: FR-06B asset-vault implementation and isolated copy/compare before any selective live cutover
